input: Resole my worn leather hiking boots

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Resoling can mean just the outsole, the midsole, the rand, or a full rebuild — the extent of the work changes cost, time, and approach entirely.
Whether the user plans to DIY or send to a cobbler/resoling service determines every step of the plan and what resources are needed.
The boot brand and current sole type (e.g., Vibram, proprietary) affects which replacement soles are compatible and which services accept the job.
Budget limits whether premium resoling services, specialty soles, or DIY kits are realistic options.
The user's location determines whether local cobblers are accessible or if mail-in resoling services must be used, affecting turnaround time.
Knowing whether the boots need to perform at the same level (e.g., serious alpine use vs. casual trails) defines how critical sole quality and bond strength are.
The user may want to replicate the original sole exactly or upgrade to a different tread pattern or compound, which shapes which sole to choose.

gold.taskDescription: The user wants to replace the worn soles on their leather hiking boots, either by doing it themselves or having it done professionally.

questions.title: Which parts of the boot need replacing — outsole only, midsole too, or full rebuild?
questions.description: Clarify the extent of wear and what the user expects to have replaced, as this determines the complexity and cost of the job.

questions.title: Do you want to DIY this or use a professional cobbler or resoling service?
questions.description: Establish whether the user will do the work themselves or outsource it, as this determines the entire approach and resource list.

questions.title: What brand and model are the boots, and what sole are they currently fitted with?
questions.description: Identify the boot make and existing sole type to determine compatible replacement options and whether the manufacturer or specialist services will accept the job.

questions.title: What is your budget for this resoling job?
questions.description: Understand the financial limit to narrow down whether premium services, standard cobblers, or budget DIY kits are appropriate.

questions.title: Do you have access to local cobblers, or would you need to mail the boots in?
questions.description: Determine geographic access to services so the plan can account for drop-off versus shipping logistics and expected turnaround time.

questions.title: What kind of hiking will these boots be used for after resoling — casual trails or demanding terrain?
questions.description: Clarify the performance requirements post-resoling to ensure the chosen sole compound and bond method are fit for purpose.

questions.title: Do you want to match the original sole exactly or switch to a different tread or compound?
questions.description: Find out whether the user wants a like-for-like replacement or an upgrade, which shapes the sole selection process.
